question: A 41-year-old man, diagnosed with bipolar disorder, who has performed an over-supply of lithium carbonate, comes to the emergency room. The exploration highlights intense tremor, ataxia, dysarthria and a vertical nystagmus. A litemia is obtained that is 4.1 mEq / L. What is the best therapeutic option?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Lithium carbonate overdose -> increased lithium levels in the blood -> symptoms of lithium toxicity (intense tremor, ataxia, dysarthria, vertical nystagmus) -> litemia of 4.1 mEq/L -> severe toxicity. -> 95%
CHAIN: Severe lithium toxicity -> urgent need for intervention -> therapeutic option required. -> 90%
CHAIN: Therapeutic option for severe lithium toxicity -> rapid elimination of lithium from the body -> improved patient outcome. -> 85%
CHAIN: Rapid elimination of lithium from the body -> Hemodialysis. -> 95%
analysis: The patient is presenting with symptoms of lithium toxicity, including tremor, ataxia, dysarthria, and nystagmus. With a lithium level of 4.1 mEq/L, the best therapeutic option is hemodialysis to remove the excess lithium from the body.
